# @workspacekit/core

> The framework-free core of the file workspace: the adapter contract, the tree store, paths, naming rules, uploads, and an HTTP client and in-memory adapter.

- API reference: https://docs-ashy-alpha.vercel.app/api/core
- Install: `npm install @workspacekit/core`

## README sections

- Install
- Entry points: `@workspacekit/core`: types, `FsError`, path helpers (`joinPath`, `parentPath`, `basename`), `createTreeStore`, `createVisibleRowIndex`, `createUploader` and the drop helpers.
- Use it on its own: `createTreeStore` wraps any `FileSystemAdapter` and subscribes to its `watch` itself.
- CSS: None.
- Options: `createTreeStore(adapter, { fetchDepth, root, onError })`: how deep each listing goes (default 2), the folder the store shows, and a callback for load failures.

## Entry points

- `@workspacekit/core`
- `@workspacekit/core/http`
- `@workspacekit/core/memory`
- `@workspacekit/core/docs`

## Exports of `@workspacekit/core`

- `CSRF_HEADER`: Request header required on every non-GET request (value `1`); a missing or different value is rejected with 403 `forbidden`.
- `CallOptions`: Options every read accepts: an `AbortSignal` that cancels the request.
- `ChangeEvent`: One change reported by `FileSystemAdapter.watch`.
- `ConflictChoice`: What to do when an upload's target already exists.
- `CreateBody`: The JSON body of `ROUTES.create`.
- `DEFAULT_SKIP`: Skips OS and tooling junk only; other dotfiles stay, because agent projects need them.
- `DownloadBody`: The JSON body of `ROUTES.download`.
- `DropEntry`: The slice of FileSystemEntry / FileSystemDirectoryEntry we use (structural, so tests can pass plain fakes).
- `DroppedItem`: What a drop handler captured synchronously: an entry still to be walked, or a plain file.
- `EntriesResponse`: The answer of `ROUTES.list` and `ROUTES.search`.
- `Entry`: One file or directory, addressed by its normalized path (`/`-separated, no leading slash, root `''`).
- `EntryKind`: Whether an entry is a file or a directory.
- `EntryResponse`: The answer of routes that return one entry.
- `ErrorBody`: The JSON body of every non-2xx response.
- `FileSystemAdapter`: The storage behind the explorer.
- `FolderNode`: One folder whose children are known (or being fetched).
- `FolderStatus`: Load state of one folder: never requested, being fetched, listed, or failed.
- `FsError`: The one error type every adapter, store and handler throws.
- `FsErrorKind`: What went wrong, independent of transport.
- `IF_MTIME_HEADER`: Request header carrying the mtime the client last saw (optimistic write check).
- `MTIME_HEADER`: Response header on `read` carrying the file's mtime.
- `NameProblem`: Why `validateName` rejects a name.
- `PollingOptions`: Options for `withPolling`: which folders to poll each round, how often, and when to pause.
- `ROUTES`: HTTP contract shared by `httpAdapter` and the server.
- `SortSpec`: How sibling entries are ordered.
- `StatResponse`: The answer of `ROUTES.stat`; `entry` is `null` for a missing path.
- `TransferBody`: The JSON body of `ROUTES.move` and `ROUTES.copy`.
- `TransferOptions`: Options for `move` and `copy`: `overwrite` replaces an existing destination instead of failing with `conflict`.
- `TreeData`: Keyed by folder path (root `''`).
- `TreeSnapshot`: An immutable view of a `TreeStore`; a new snapshot (with a higher `version`) follows every change.
- `TreeStore`: The tree state for one adapter, created by `createTreeStore`.
- `TreeStoreOptions`: Options of `createTreeStore`.
- `TreeTransferOptions`: Options for `TreeStore.move` and `TreeStore.copy`: the adapter's `TransferOptions` plus the destination name.
- `UploadCompleteBody`: The JSON body of `ROUTES.uploadComplete`.
- `UploadInitBody`: The JSON body of `ROUTES.uploadInit`.
- `UploadInitResponse`: The answer to `ROUTES.uploadInit`: the session id and the chunk size the client must use.
- `UploadItem`: `relativePath` includes the file name and is untrusted.
- `UploadOptions`: Options for one `upload` run.
- `UploadProgress`: Progress of an upload run, reported after every change.
- `UploadResult`: The outcome of an upload run, per file.
- `UploadTransport`: How an adapter sends file bytes: always `direct`, and `chunked` for large files when the server supports it.
- `Uploader`: Uploads files and folders, created by `createUploader`.
- `UploaderOptions`: How an uploader sends files and checks for existing ones.
- `VisibleRow`: One row of the flattened tree, with everything a renderer needs for ARIA attributes.
- `VisibleRowIndex`: Random access to the rows `flattenVisible` would produce, without materializing them.
- `WatchFrame`: Payload of one SSE `data:` line.
- `WatchOptions`: Hints a caller gives `FileSystemAdapter.watch`.
- `basename`: The last path segment.
- `captureDataTransfer`: Call synchronously inside the drop handler: the entries are invalid once the handler returns.
- `createTreeStore`: The tree state for one adapter: folder listings, load errors, pending mutations and paths changed by others, as an external store for `useSyncExternalStore`.
- `createUploader`: An uploader over an `UploadTransport`.
- `createVisibleRowIndex`: The rendering path for the tree: a virtualized list asks for `count`, `rowAt(i)` for the rows on screen, `indexOf` to scroll to a path, and `ancestorsAt` for sticky headers.
- `entryAt`: The entry at `path`, if its parent folder is loaded; always `undefined` for the root.
- `expandDropped`: Walks dropped folders into upload items, breadth-first with 8 directory reads in flight.
- `extname`: Lowercase, no dot; `''` for dotfiles and extensionless names.
- `fromFileList`: Upload items for the files of an `<input type="file">`, keeping folder paths from `webkitdirectory` inputs.
- `isFsError`: Whether `error` is an `FsError`.
- `isSameOrDescendant`: Whether `path` is `ancestor` or lies below it.
- `joinPath`: Joins path parts and normalizes the result.
- `normalizePath`: Canonical form: NFC, `/`-separated, no leading/trailing slash, no `.`/`..`.
- `parentPath`: The parent folder's path; `''` for top-level entries and for the root.
- `parseRoute`: Splits a `ROUTES` value into its HTTP method and its path below the base URL.
- `remapPrefix`: Moves `path` from below `from` to below `to`; paths outside `from` are returned unchanged.
- `sortedChildren`: `node`'s children in display order, memoized until the node's children change.
- `splitName`: `ext` includes the dot; leading-dot names (`.env`) and extensionless names have `ext: ''`.
- `statusForKind`: The HTTP status the server answers for an error kind (500 for kinds without one).
- `statusOf`: The load status of the folder at `path` (`'idle'` when it has no node).
- `toFsError`: Converts anything thrown into an `FsError`: aborts become `cancelled`, fetch network failures (`TypeError`) become `network`, and everything else `unknown`, keeping the original as `cause`.
- `uniqueName`: `name` if it is free among `taken`, else the first free `name copy`, `name copy 2`, … keeping the extension.
- `validateName`: Checks a new entry name against `siblings`.
- `validateTransfer`: `from` and `toDir` must be normalized paths.
- `withPolling`: Adds `watch` to an adapter that has none by diffing depth-1 listings into ChangeEvents (actor 'external').

## Exports of `@workspacekit/core/http`

- `HttpAdapterOptions`: Options for `httpAdapter`: a custom `fetch`, extra headers (or a function returning them), credentials and watch behavior.
- `httpAdapter`: A `FileSystemAdapter` speaking the `ROUTES` protocol to a server made with `createFileHandler`.

## Exports of `@workspacekit/core/memory`

- `MemoryAdapter`: An in-memory `FileSystemAdapter` that can also `emit` change events, as if made by someone else.
- `MemoryAdapterOptions`: Options for `createMemoryAdapter`: seed files, artificial latency and the chunk size it reports.
- `createMemoryAdapter`: A complete `FileSystemAdapter` kept in memory, for tests, demos and prototypes.

## Exports of `@workspacekit/core/docs`

- `DOCS_URL`: The documentation site's address, in one place so the examples, the site, the generated files and the error messages agree.
- `docsLink`: The address of a documentation page, and of a heading on it, for error messages that point at the fix.
